{{Article header|deck=Hub for asteroid and planetary surface mining methods, equipment, locations, procedures, and market planning.}}

'''Mining''' covers resource extraction from asteroids and planetary deposits in ''Elite Dangerous''. Traditional asteroid mining uses ship-mounted tools, limpets, and a refinery to produce cargo; Live 4.4.1 also adds planetary [[Surface Mining]] with the [[Rhino]] Surface Recon Vehicle.<ref name="frontier-getting-started">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/getting-started-elite-dangerous Getting Started in Elite Dangerous], Frontier Developments, accessed 2026-09-10.</ref><ref name="frontier-rhino-update">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/updates/4-4-1-0 Elite Dangerous — 4.4.1.0 Update Notes], Frontier Developments, 3 September 2026.</ref>

Use this hub to choose a method and reach its reference pages or Field Procedures. Complete extraction sequences, troubleshooting, equipment specifications, and vehicle details are available through the linked pages.

== Start here ==

An asteroid-mining run usually has five parts:

# choose a mining method and fit the ship for that method;
# bring enough limpets and cargo space for the planned run;
# travel to a suitable [[Planetary Rings|planetary ring]], [[Mining Hotspot|hotspot]], or known mining location;
# prospect, extract, collect, and refine the desired resources; and
# check current market data before selling the cargo.

New commanders can begin with [[How to Start Mining]]. Planetary Surface Mining uses a different preparation and extraction loop; begin with [[Surface Mining]] or the complete [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]] procedure.

== Field Procedures ==

{{#invoke:Procedures|list|topic=Mining}}

== Asteroid mining methods ==

{{#invoke:Mining|methodsTable}}

Each method has its own complete procedure. A combined fit can carry more than one set of extraction tools, but every additional tool competes for hardpoints, internals, power, and cargo capacity.

== Asteroid-mining equipment ==

{{#invoke:Mining|equipmentTable}}

A mining ship normally carries an extraction tool, collector support, a refinery, cargo space, and enough limpets for the planned run. The exact layout depends on the method: a laser miner does not need seismic charges, while a dedicated core miner uses a pulse wave analyser, seismic charges, and an abrasion blaster.

The equipment map follows the module names used by the EDCD Coriolis and FDevIDs datasets.<ref name="edcd-coriolis">[https://github.com/EDCD/coriolis-data EDCD Coriolis data], Elite Dangerous Community Developers, accessed 2026-09-10.</ref><ref name="edcd-fdevids">[https://github.com/EDCD/FDevIDs EDCD FDevIDs], Elite Dangerous Community Developers, accessed 2026-09-10.</ref>

== Planetary Surface Mining ==

Surface Mining is a Live-only activity introduced with the Rhino update. The Rhino detects planetary mining deposits, deploys mining rigs, and refines the recovered resources. The [[Surface Mining]] reference article explains the mechanic and associated equipment; [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]] covers the full working procedure.<ref name="frontier-rhino-update" />

== Asteroid locations and search concepts ==

{{#invoke:Mining|locationConcepts}}

Most ship-based mining happens in [[Planetary Rings|planetary rings]]. A [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] reveals ring hotspots, but the named hotspot is a search aid rather than a guaranteed result; prospect individual asteroids before committing extraction time.

== Commodity planning ==

Asteroid fragments and deposits become cargo after processing through a refinery. Prices and demand vary between markets and over time, so check current data before travelling to sell. [[Tools and Resources]] lists community services commonly used for current market and route information.
